data.title: TAIEX falls below 40,000 points
data.description:
US ELECTIONS FALLOUT: Bargain hunters stepped in after the intraday low, while the government yesterday authorized activation of the National Stabilization Fund

Shares in Taiwan yesterday suffered their fourth-largest single-day point loss, closing below the 40,000-point mark following an overnight sell-off on Wall Street, although the market recovered from its intraday low on hopes of government measures to support stocks.

The TAIEX closed down 1,873.08 points, or 4.51 percent, at 39,701.64 after plunging by about 3,700 points in early trading as artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks led the decline.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電), which accounts for more than 40 percent of the market’s total capitalization, recovered from an earlier 10 percent decline to close down 4.69 percent at NT$2,135.

Turnover on the main board totaled NT$1.246 trillion (US$38.02 billion), up from the previous session’s NT$926.024 billion, Taiwan Stock Exchange data showed.

Foreign institutional investors sold a net NT$91.19 billion of shares on the main board yesterday and have sold a net NT$705.658 billion over the past seven sessions, the data showed.

Yesterday’s market sell-off followed losses on Wall Street amid concerns over possible restrictions on AI data center development after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress and won gubernatorial contests over Republican rivals in states including Texas, a major data center hub, in Tuesday’s midterm elections.

“After the TAIEX hit its intraday low, however, bargain hunters stepped in around noon, easing the selling pressure as the Financial Supervisory Commission [FSC] said it would convene a meeting later today [yesterday] to discuss possible market supporting measures,” Moore Securities Investment Consulting Co (摩爾投顧) analyst Adam Lin (林漢偉) said.

In addition, the government yesterday authorized the activation of its NT$500 billion National Stabilization Fund to support local shares.

“The government’s statements reassured some investors, encouraging them to buy on the dip,” Lin said.

“Despite the rebound from the day’s low, it is too early to tell when the TAIEX will climb out of the current doldrums,” he said. “Pay close attention to what the FSC will come up with to support the market.”

Yesterday’s sell-off came after New York’s NASDAQ Composite Index plunged 5.5 percent in its worst day — percentage-wise — since April last year when US President Donald Trump unveiled his wide-ranging global tariffs.

The S&P 500 tanked more than 4 percent and the Dow Jones Industrial Average more than 3 percent.

Bloomberg reported that the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had collapsed about 16 percent this week, putting it on course for its worst run since April last year.

Trading boards were a sea of red across Asia. Seoul briefly plunged almost 9 percent before closing 6 percent lower, with chip giant SK Hynix Inc off more than 10 percent and rival Samsung Electronics Co down 6.4 percent.

The KOSPI more than doubled between the end of December last year and the middle of June, when it hit a record, and has since then lost almost 50 percent.

Tokyo dived 6 percent as Softbank Group Corp gave back more than 10 percent, with Kioxia Holdings Corp off 8.7 percent and Advantest Corp 5 percent lower.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Jakarta, Bangkok, Wellington and Manila were also in the red.

Additional reporting by AFP

data.title: Bank of America advises NT dollar buys
data.description:
‘LONG ON NT’: An official said the NT dollar was the Asian currency most correlated with AI exchange-traded funds, making its drop consistent with a positioning squeeze

The New Taiwan dollar and the South Korean won offer buying opportunities after the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven equity selloff, a Bank of America Corp executive said in an interview released yesterday.

Both currencies have weakened in tandem with AI-linked stocks, but the size of their current-account surpluses gives investors “substantial” cover to build long positions, said Claudio Piron, head of Asia foreign-exchange and rates strategy at Bank of America’s global research unit.

“That will come into play,” he told Bloomberg TV. “I would say at the margin that these levels here provide an opportunity for people to enter into long [South] Korean won positions and long Taiwan positions.”

Piron said the NT dollar was the Asian currency most correlated with AI exchange-traded funds, making its recent decline consistent with a positioning squeeze rather than a fundamental deterioration.

The NT dollar fell as much as 0.5 percent to NT$33.040 per US dollar in early session yesterday, making it Asia’s worst performer.

However, the local currency reversed its earlier losses and turned stronger against the US dollar later yesterday. It gained NT$0.108, or 0.33 percent, to close at NT$32.768 in Taipei trading.

With the NT dollar rarely trading beyond NT$33 versus the US dollar over the past decade, authorities are likely to stay vigilant, although their focus will remain on smoothing volatility rather than defending a specific level, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp (華僑銀行) foreign exchange strategist Christopher Wong (黃經隆) said.

“Near term, we expect the [New] Taiwan dollar to remain volatile, with equity market performance and foreign portfolio flows likely to dominate FX direction,” Wong said, adding that the currency risks sliding toward NT$33.3 per US dollar.

Morning outflows by foreign funds were cushioned at about midday by aggressive exporter US dollar sales, according to local foreign-exchange traders.

As domestic stocks pared losses, state-owned banks stepped up US dollar sales, pushing the currency pair back below the NT$33 mark, said the traders, who asked not to be identified as they are not allowed to speak publicly.

The central bank recently eased restrictions on US dollar sales by exporters to reduce depreciation pressure on the NT dollar and encouraged exporters with conversion needs to sell US dollars rather than wait for a better rate.

data.title: Google to build Wyoming facility
data.description:
Alphabet Inc’s Google on Thursday said it would spend US$17 billion to build a data center in Wyoming, formally putting a price tag on the proposal two days after voters across the US delivered a broad rebuke to the development of such massive projects for artificial intelligence (AI) work.

Voters in Tuesday’s US midterm elections sided with limits on data centers in 40 of 41 local ballot measures, according to Ballotpedia.

In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor’s race after promising a data center moratorium.

Successful Democratic candidates for governor in Georgia, Ohio and Pennsylvania also campaigned on stricter regulations of the projects.

Google said in a blog post that the facility in Laramie County, Wyoming, would be its first in the state.

The company said it would pay for all the power the data center uses.

Last month, American Electric Power Co said it planned to invest US$4 billion in the project, which is to draw electricity in part from a 702 megawatt natural gas fuel cell development built with Bloom Energy Corp fuel cells.

The project would be air-cooled to limit water use, it added.

The deal reflects growing interest from technology companies in Bloom’s fuel cells as they look to provide power for energy-hungry AI systems.

Natural gas turbines are back-ordered for years, and nuclear projects can take a decade or more to permit and build.

Bloom said its fuel cells can be installed in as little as 90 days.

Google also said it expects to generate hundreds of millions of dollars in local property taxes and will form a community council with its partners to address growth concerns in Cheyenne, Wyoming.

Meanwhile, about 40 percent of pending data center capacity in the US is planned to be built in states where newly elected governors have promised to stop or pause such construction, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence company.

That is on top of 46 local ballot measures approved or on track to pass that also stall development, according to Bloomberg Economics.

At least 17 of those are outright bans on large-scale data centers.

Hyperscalers, the largest cloud-computing providers, are expected to overhaul and shift development plans in response.

Tuesday’s election results stand to shrink the US$1.4 trillion that technology companies were expected to spend on AI infrastructure by roughly 5 to 7 percent next year, Bloomberg Intelligence technology analyst Mandeep Singh said.

That includes spending on chips, networking equipment, land and other materials for data center construction, Singh said.

The cuts and the anticipated slowdown in approvals might translate into as many as 10 gigawatts of data center capacity failing to come online next year as planned, he said.

“We’ve gone from the question of who is going to pass a moratorium to where can I even construct one of these things now?” Bloomberg Intelligence policy analyst Justin Teresi said.

GLJ Research LLC founder Gordon Johnson said in a note on Tuesday that Texas data center projects that do not already have electricity and environmental permits lined up would “probably go to Louisiana, Oklahoma or nowhere.”

data.title: Foreign exchange reserves dip below US$600 billion
data.description:
Taiwan’s foreign exchange reserves fell below US$600 billion at the end of last month as the central bank intervened in the currency market, selling US dollars and buying New Taiwan dollars to ease volatility in the local currency.

Taiwan’s foreign exchange reserves totaled US$596.437 billion at the end of last month, down US$4.308 billion from the end of September, declining for a second consecutive month, the central bank said in a statement released on Thursday.

Investment returns and exchange rate movements involving other currencies helped support foreign exchange reserves last month, Department of Foreign Exchange Director-General Eugene Tsai (蔡炯民) said.

Nonetheless, the NT dollar fell NT$0.626, or 1.93 percent, against the US dollar during the month amid a stock market sell-off and massive foreign fund outflows, prompting the central bank to intervene, Tsai said.

Foreign institutional investors withdrew a record net US$28 billion last month, including the repatriation of cash dividends, Tsai said, citing central bank data.

During the month, the TAIEX fell 2,728.30 points, or 5.67 percent, amid concerns over spending on artificial intelligence (AI).

The central bank remained committed to keeping Taiwan’s foreign exchange market stable, Tsai said.

He cited heavy net selling by foreign institutional investors during several trading sessions last month, including one session when net sales reached NT$300 billion (US$9.16 billion), sending the NT dollar sharply lower and prompting central bank intervention.

The central bank also received substantial interest payments from its holdings of US Treasury securities through swap transactions last month, helping offset the impact of its market intervention in the foreign exchange market, he said.

Foreign investors held US$1.743 trillion in Taiwan-listed stocks, bonds and NT dollar deposits, down from US$1.927 trillion at the end of September, central bank data showed.

The holdings were equivalent to 292 percent of Taiwan’s total foreign exchange reserves last month, compared with 321 percent a month earlier.

Analysts said the decline in foreign investors’ holdings reflected weakness in the local stock market.

The central bank has said it would maintain ample foreign exchange reserves to ensure the stability of domestic financial markets and guard against sudden capital outflows by foreign institutional investors.

data.title: Catcher Technology optimistic about its components sector
data.description:
Metal casing supplier Catcher Technology Co (可成科技) yesterday said it is optimistic about its precision components business, with products for artificial intelligence (AI) servers, medical technology, semiconductor automation, aerospace and drones entering volume shipments.

However, the company has faced order cuts for products used in notebook computers over the past two years, making operating conditions challenging, Catcher chairman Allen Hung (洪水樹) told an earnings conference.

Catcher supplies mechanical and external parts for servers, as well as power supply products and switches.

AI-related products accounted for a double-digit percentage of Catcher’s total revenue in the third quarter and are on track to reach about 20 percent for the full year, Hung said.

As more products for AI servers enter mass production, the segment’s revenue contribution is expected to increase further this quarter and in the first quarter next year, Catcher said.

The company has invested US$50 million in Thailand over the past two years, focusing mainly on AI server-related products, it said.

AI PC-related projects are also scheduled to enter mass production in the second quarter of next year, it said.

Overall, the revenue share of AI-related products could surpass that of the notebook business next year, it said.

This year, precision components for medical equipment, aviation engines and uncrewed vehicles, and AI-related products are each expected to account for about 20 percent of Catcher’s total revenue, with the remainder coming from notebook business, the company said.

Catcher remains cautious about its notebook business through next year due to component shortages and rising prices, with revenue from the segment already down by a double-digit percentage in the first three quarters of this year, Hung said.

The company yesterday reported that third-quarter revenue rose 15.2 percent quarter-on-quarter, but fell 36.5 percent year-on-year to NT$3.09 billion (US$94.3 million).

Net profit fell 4.3 percent quarter-on-quarter and 55 percent year-on-year to NT$1.3 billion.

Earnings per share fell to NT$2.45 from NT$2.51 in the previous quarter and NT$4.62 a year earlier.

Gross margin fell to 22 percent last quarter from 28.86 percent in the second quarter and 28.6 percent a year earlier, mainly as repeated cuts in notebook orders forced the company to focus on inventory reduction, Hung said.

Catcher aims to restore its gross margin to about 30 percent in the long term, supported by an expected expansion in semiconductor automation equipment components next year and new uncrewed vehicle projects with US customers, he said.

data.title: AI boom turns chip packaging into the next battleground for semiconductors
data.description:
A global race to build artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is unleashing billions of dollars of investment in advanced chip packaging, a once unglamorous aspect of technology that has become a critical bottleneck in turning out the world’s most powerful processors.

As demand for AI chips outstrips available packaging capacity, companies from Nvidia Corp and Advanced Micro Devices Inc (AMD) to lesser-known players in Taiwan are expanding production, while equipment makers develop new tools, interviews with more than a dozen industry executives and analysts show.

"Packaging was always that thing that you just didn’t worry about," former Intel Corp chief executive officer Pat Gelsinger, now a partner at Playground Global LLC, told reporters in Taipei recently.

Advanced packaging could eventually account for as much as half the value of a chip product, Gelsinger estimated, as some of today’s graphics and central processing units can integrate 10 or more chips, sometimes as many as 20.

Revenue from advanced packaging is forecast to overtake that earned via the traditional route for the first time this year, says research firm Yole Group, with capital spending on the technology expected to near US$28 billion.

TAIWAN FIRM DOMINATES CHIP-ON-WAFER SUBSTRATE

The world’s largest contract chipmaker, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電), dominates the most sophisticated advanced packaging technology, including chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS).

The technology links separate pieces of silicon, such as processors and memory chips, on a shared base, to let them work together at high speed.

It is widely used by Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom Inc, as well as cloud companies developing their own AI chips.

But TSMC’s capacity limits have spurred some chip designers to seek additional supply.

Nvidia, for example, is providing billions of dollars in financing to expand CoWoS packaging capacity at Siliconware Precision Industries Co (SPIL, 矽品精密), a unit of ASE Technology Holding Co (ASE, 日月光投控), said an industry executive familiar with the matter, who sought anonymity for lack of authorisation to talk to media.

The funding will support new factory space and equipment, the executive said. The scale of the support has not previously been reported.

Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. ASE said it does not comment on market rumours involving its customers.

A FUNDAMENTAL CHIPMAKING SHIFT

The scramble to invest reflects a broader change in manufacturing of powerful chips, as more chip designers use advanced packaging to integrate multiple chips, such as processors and memory, into a single package.

That allows the ensemble to work together faster as one system, in contrast with the practice of decades, when packaging served mainly to protect chips and provide the electrical connections to attach them to circuit boards.

The shift comes as it become harder and costlier to win performance gains by shrinking and adding transistors, the tiny switches inside a chip.

The newer packaging technique is especially important for AI chips, which need to shuffle vast amounts of data between processors and nearby memory. Speeding up such transfers hastens the process of training and running AI models.

A RACE FOR TSMC ALTERNATIVES

TSMC’s tight capacity offers an opportunity for smaller suppliers, such as Powertech Technology Inc (力成科技).

"Everyone is looking for a solution outside TSMC," Powertech chairman Tsai Du-kung (蔡篤恭) told reporters in August. "They don’t want to rely entirely on TSMC."

Powertech is betting on panel-level packaging, which uses larger rectangular panels instead of round wafers as the chip packaging platform.

This way, it can accommodate more chips in each production run and waste less material, an advantage as AI processors become larger and more complex.

Powertech is working with AMD and Broadcom on the technology as the industry seeks to demonstrate its viability for larger, more complex chip packages used in AI and high-performance computing.

"The most important thing right now is capacity," Powertech senior vice president Jim Lin (林基正) said, adding that customers were waiting for the company to ramp up production.

Powertech plans to invest US$400 million in an advanced packaging joint venture with Broadcom in Singapore. Production could begin in 2028, Tsai said.

To support larger and more complex chip packages, TSMC is developing its own panel-based technology, called chip-on-panel-on-substrate (CoPoS).

In April, the company said it had built a CoPoS pilot line and expected production to begin within a couple of years, but CoWoS remains TSMC’s main AI-packaging technology.

AMD has also unveiled investments of more than US$10 billion across Taiwan’s semiconductor industry, including partnerships with ASE, SPIL and Powertech on advanced packaging.

Asked if Powertech’s panel-level packaging technology could offer an alternative to TSMC’s technology, AMD chief executive officer Lisa Su (蘇姿丰) did not directly address the question but acknowledged the need for more advanced packaging capacity.

"I think CoWoS and advanced packaging are super important for our high-performance computing going forward," Su told Reuters in Taipei last month.

"TSMC has been an incredible partner in advanced packaging, and we’re going to continue to do more together. And yes, we do need more capacity overall."

Panel-level packaging would reduce material waste when packaging larger AI chips, said Microsoft Azure hardware chief Rani Borkar, though the company has not decided whether or when it will adopt the technology.

CHIP EQUIPMENT MAKERS JOIN THE RUSH

The packaging boom is also opening a new market for makers of semiconductor equipment.

Such companies have traditionally focused on earlier stages of chipmaking, when circuitry is built onto silicon. Advanced packaging comes later, when chips, memory or other components are joined into a finished high-performance unit.

Advanced packaging was growing much faster than the market for chip-making gear, though it remained smaller, Tokyo Electron Taiwan Ltd president Seiji Nakama said.

The market for advanced packaging, including panel-level technology, could grow significantly within three to five years, an official at US equipment maker Applied Materials Inc said.

"It’s near-term," said Sree Kesapragada, a vice president at the company, which is increasingly focusing on the new format. "It’s not like, 10 years, 15 years off."

data.title: Macronix mulls capacity expansion
data.description:
‘DIFFERENT APPROACH’: Company chairman Miin Wu said it would not recklessly chase expansion and prefers to invest in new products to hedge against bubble risks

Macronix International Co (旺宏電子), a major supplier of NOR and NAND flash memory chips, on Wednesday said that it is cautiously evaluating capacity expansion to navigate the memory industry’s prolonged supply-driven upcycle through 2030.

Robust demand for artificial intelligence (AI) servers and AI-related applications has led to a crowding-out effect on production of less-advanced memory chips and a supply crunch, the Hsinchu-based chipmaker said.

To meet the demand, major chip suppliers have announced a slew of new capacity expansion plans, it said.

Macronix’s local peer Winbond Electronics Corp (華邦電子), the world’s largest NOR flash memory chipmaker, on Tuesday announced that it had approved capital expenditure of NT$73.2 billion (US$2.23 billion) for its Kaohsiung fab expansion and production equipment.

The announcement came after Winbond in September clinched a deal to acquire Infineon Technologies’ NOR Flash and F-RAM business for US$1.12 billion.

Asked about its capacity expansion strategy, Macronix chairman Miin Wu (吳敏求) said that it has no intention to “build a new plant.”

Instead, the company prioritizes boosting factory utilization to full capacity, Wu said.

“Macronix is never a ‘me too’ company. Macronix likes to create [new] ideas,” he said.

Asked whether Macronix is scouting potential acquisition deals to rapidly boost capacity, Wu said: “We all have a vision, right? How to realize it will depend on one’s abilities.”

“We will definitely take a different approach,” he said. “We will not invest recklessly as other companies did.”

As Macronix’s factories are approaching full usage, it is counting on price increases rather than capacity addition to drive rapid revenue growth, the company said.

Any new capacity addition would take at least one year, it said.

The chip shortage is expected to extend into 2030, Wu said.

Macronix expects to add 5,000 12-inch wafers per month through a NT$15.8 billion investment, but it would not add to wafer capacity until 2028, mainly due to longer-than-expected equipment lead time, the company said.

Concerns over a potential AI bubble are mounting, with investors fearing that large-scale US cloud service providers might fail to translate their massive infrastructure investments into reasonable returns, Wu said.

At this juncture, strategic precision in capacity investment is critical for companies and Macronix prefers to invest in new product developments to hedge against AI bubble risks, he said.

The company has several new products in the pipeline for release next year, he added.

As a chipmaker capable of producing satellite-grade components, Macronix has secured a key deal to supply NOR and eMMC NAND flash memory to SpaceX for its low Earth orbit satellite constellations, Wu said.

The partnership is expected to boost the company’s annual shipment volume by more than 1 million units, he said.

Meanwhile, at a forum organized by National Cheng Kung University yesterday, Wu said he plans to donate US$2 million to establish a fund to foster talent.

His initial plan is that the fund will provide scholarships to support outstanding interdisciplinary students from National Cheng Kung University to study at Stanford University in California, he said.

data.title: CSC announces domestic prices to rise next month
data.description:
China Steel Corp (CSC, 中鋼), Taiwan’s largest integrated steelmaker, yesterday announced that it is increasing domestic prices next month, amid price rises overseas, robust orders and depreciation of the New Taiwan dollar.

The announcement came as raw material costs remain relatively high, with iron ore and metallurgical coal prices at about US$90 and US$265 per tonne respectively, keeping steelmaking costs relatively high, CSC said in a statement.

China’s output curbs, along with protectionist trade policies in the US and Europe, have led to tighter supply and higher steel prices, it said.

In the US, hot-rolled coil spot prices recently climbed above US$1,450 per tonne, the highest in nearly four-and-a-half years, while Tokyo Steel Manufacturing Co last month raised its prices for hot-rolled coils, rebar and I-beams by ￥3,000 (US$18.94) per tonne.

Hung Yen, Vietnam-based Hoa Phat Group’s hot-rolled coil prices were also up by US$5 per tonne due to exchange rate factors, CSC said.

“Global steel prices are showing a steady upward trend,” the statement said.

Against this backdrop, the Kaohsiung-based company is raising prices by NT$300 (US$9.13) per tonne, its third consecutive monthly increase, it said.

The price hikes apply to products such as hot-rolled steel plates and coils, cold-rolled steel coils, anti-fingerprint electro-galvanized steel coils, hot-dip galvanized coils for construction and coating, and electro-galvanized coils for construction, it said.

CSC’s cumulative revenue in the first three quarters of this year rose 6.16 percent year-on-year to NT$256.67 billion amid robust domestic demand and a recovering global steel market.

Analysts at Yuanta Securities Investment Consulting Co (元大投顧) said in a note that CSC’s price hikes could see this quarter’s revenue increase 20 percent to NT$90.46 billion from a year earlier.

With full-year revenue estimated to rise 9.5 percent annually to NT$347.14 billion, the company is forecast to turn profitable this year with net profit of NT$2.77 billion after reporting a net loss of NT$4.35 billion last year, its first loss in 47 years, Yuanta said.

data.title: Global AI server shipments expected to jump 36%
data.description:
SERVER TAKEOVER? A researcher said an increase in capital expenditure by CSPs reflects higher procurements and prices for memory, GPUs and AI server systems

Global artificial intelligence (AI) server shipments are expected to rise 36 percent year-on-year to 3.83 million units next year, as nine major cloud service providers (CSPs) in China and the US continue their robust investments in AI infrastructure, TrendForce Corp (集邦科技) said yesterday.

The nine major CSPs’ combined capital expenditure is projected to rise 60 percent year-on-year to US$1.52 trillion next year, despite market concerns and geopolitical tensions, TrendForce research manager Frank Kung (龔明德) told a forum in Taipei.

The nine CSPs are Alphabet Inc’s Google, Amazon.com Inc, Meta Platforms Inc, Microsoft Corp, Oracle Corp, ByteDance Ltd (字節跳動), Tencent Holdings (騰訊), Alibaba Group Holding (阿里巴巴) and Baidu Inc (百度).

The increase in capital expenditure reflects higher procurements and rising prices across the supply chain, from memory chips and graphics processing units (GPUs) to AI server systems, Kung said.

Next year, the AI server market is expected to grow 92 percent to US$919 billion, accounting for 81 percent of the overall server market value, he said.

Nvidia is expected to remain the dominant AI server supplier next year, with shipments of 100,000 racks and a market share of 62.6 percent, he added.

As adoption broadens and supply improves, shipments of Nvidia’s Vera Rubin racks could expand further and overtake the GB series in the second quarter of next year, accounting for about 70 percent of Nvidia’s total rack shipments for the year, Kung said.

By contrast, shipments of server racks based on Nvidia’s next-generation Rubin Ultra platform are expected to remain limited, accounting for only a single-digit percentage of the chipmaker’s total rack shipments next year, he said.

TrendForce has reported growing demand from CSPs for Advanced Micro Devices Inc’s (AMD) Helios systems in the AI server market, Kung said.

Demand for the Helios systems is about 5,000 racks this year and the number could double next year, although deployment and delivery challenges could limit the conversion of orders into shipments, he said.

Helios could face similar, or even greater, ramp-up challenges than Nvidia’s new platforms because it is AMD’s first rack-scale design, meaning it would take time for customer demand to translate into actual deliveries, Kung added.
